question.text: Per the workbook, for a scheme in existence for more than six months but less than one year, performance advertisements must provide returns as __________.

answer.text: Simple annualized growth rate for the past 6 months

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that for schemes in existence for more than six months but less than one year, performance advertisements must provide the simple annualized growth rate for the past six months. For schemes in existence for less than six months, past performance figures should not be provided at all. The Trap: The workbook does not endorse a blanket rule that any period under one year must be shown as an absolute return; the sub-six-month rule is "no past performance" rather than "absolute return". Compounded annualization (CAGR) is reserved for longer periods. Note: When discussing recent-launch schemes with investors, follow the workbook's two-step rule: under six months means no past performance figure, six months to one year means simple annualized growth.
